newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum steady, cotton crop good - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum steady, cotton crop good - Grainco.

text.p: Australian and international sorghum markets remained fundamentally unchanged in the past week, Queensland grain co-operative Grainco said on Monday in its weekly market report.

Trading manager Rob Brealey said late harvest in southern Queensland and some early harvest in central Queensland brought some grower selling, but tonnage traded on a daily basis remained relatively small compared with previous years.
Domestic values in southern Queensland were steady to a little softer over the week and the April market appeared fairly comfortable with its requirements, he said.
In central Queensland, values reflected the volatility of the export market as Chicago futures reacted in the lead-up to corn planting in the U.S.

Domestic values finished the week around A$151.00 a tonne Brisbane for April delivery, while the later months continued to attract a premium over nearby months reflecting some of the carry costs involved in storing the grain.
In central Queensland the market finished the week at around A$132.00 a tonne delivered port for April delivery.

Based on last week's 500,000 tonnes of feed barley purchases by Saudi Arabia, which went to Europe and Canada and with Australia unlikely to have participated, Australian domestic feed barley values continued to trade a premium over export values, he said.
Tonnage traded domestically over the past week again appeared relatively small, with late week reports of a parcel trading at around the equivalent of A$156.00-A$157.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane.
The market was quite in cottonseed during the week with the onset of picking absorbing most growers' time.
Dryland yields remain a concern across the Darling Downs region of Queensland but this was not unexpected because of lack of moisture during the growing season, he said.
Irrigators were yet to make a significant start on picking and once they commence yields are expected to improve, he said.

Ginning was underway in all cotton growing areas and yields were showing that the cotton had stood up well to the mild season. Earlier suggestions that the crop production may be further reduced have now given way with the output likely to make 2.5 million 500-pound bales or a little better, he said.

Export markets firmed slightly during the week as international consumers make further coverage. Domestically prices fluctuated over the the week as early seed was aggressively pursued. With this push satisfied, prices settled in the mid A$130.00 a tonne ex gin.
Most oilseed markets finished the week slightly softer despite bullish news from the USDA on tight soy ending stocks.

Australian domestic prices remained fairly stable over the week. Sunflowers were steady at A$310.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane for April 1997 and A$315.00 delivered Newcastle for April. Central Queensland new crop black sunflower prices were

A$295.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane or around A$250.00-A$255.00 a tonne delivered central Queensland depot for May-July 1997. New crop soybean prices were still trading at A$412.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane.
